title: Prefill queue throttling and attention-kernel fallback policy to mitigate v2/v3 FlashAttention regressions
creator: Priya Nair
description: Summary: After the FlashAttention v3 rollout to the public model catalog we observed intermittent p95 decode latency regressions and throughput drops for short to medium sequence workloads. Regression pattern is correlated with high prefill concurrency and requests that oscillate between prefill-heavy and decode-heavy phases (chat-style traffic). Hypothesis: v3 kernel selection is superior for long contiguous prefill work but interacts poorly with our prefill->decode scheduling under high concurrency, causing frequent kernel fallback churn and suboptimal kernel selection at decode time. This ticket scopes an investigation and mitigation that adds prefill queue backpressure (throttling) and a deterministic kernel fallback policy tuned by KV cache hit-rate and token position to stabilize latency and avoid thrash.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce the p95 regression in a controlled harness with <=10% variance across runs
Implement prefill queue throttling that reduces end-to-end p95 latency by >=20% for affected workloads in our synthetic tests
Introduce a kernel-fallback policy that avoids >3 kernel switches per request on average and reduces fallback-related stalls
Benchmark matrix (seq_len 16/64/512, batch 1/8/32) shows no regression in throughput or p50 latency vs current baseline across NVIDIA A100 and H100 profiles
Code changes covered by unit tests and an integration test in our perf CI; change documented in runtime-1.22 release notes
experiments: 2025-02-13: Baseline runs on perf harness (catalog:v3-default) - p95 decode latency spike observed for seq<=64, batch>=8. Repro rate ~85% under synthetic chat mix (prefill:decode ratio 1.2). Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/perf/runs/ENG-20567-baseline

2025-02-14: A/B test: force FlashAttn v2 for short sequence paths - p95 improved by 28% but long-seq throughput regressed 6% in heavy prefill workload. Notes saved to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/ENG-20567/ab-v2
2025-02-16: Implemented simple prefill queue token-leak based throttling (alpha) and ran 6 trials. Observed 22-31% p95 improvement, decode p50 stable. Regression on long-seq reduced to 1-2%.

2025-02-18: Evaluated kernel-fallback policy that factors KV cache hit ratio and token_index%32: reduced kernel thrash events from 12->2 per 1000 requests. End-to-end p95 improved further. Experimental harness: https://dash.redwood/perf/runs/ENG-20567-throttle-fallback

2025-02-19: Stress test under mixed-tenant workload (multi-model): prefill throttling introduced mild tail latency increases for unrelated tenants; mitigation: per-tenant throttling limits and burst tokens (proposal below).
decisions: Adopt combined mitigations: conservative prefill queue backpressure + deterministic kernel-fallback policy. Rationale: gives most stable improvement across sequence distributions without permanently disabling v3 kernels.
Do not revert v3 globally. Rolling back v3 causes unacceptable long-seq throughput regressions for larger customers.
Implement per-tenant burst capacity tokens so throttling affects only noisy tenants rather than cluster-wide throughput.
next_steps: Ship prefill queue throttling feature-flag behind runtime-1.22 flag and enable for canary cluster (canary:region-us-west-2) - owner: Diego
Merge deterministic kernel-fallback policy (policy uses KV cache hit-rate threshold=0.6 and token_pos_threshold=48) - owner: SRE/infra pair
Add observability: histogram of kernel-switches-per-request, KV-cache-hit ratio per request, and prefill-queue-wait-time per tenant
Run 3-day soak in canary with real traffic and monitor p95 and kernel-switch metrics; roll-forward if stable
Follow-up: refine thresholds based on production telemetry and add autotuning entrypoint (future ticket)
